unanimous

yoo-NAN-uh-mus -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, NAN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unanimous is fully in agreement from all parties.

The judges' decision was unanimous: all five scorecards named the same winner.

Example

When the club votes on its new mascot, the choice is unanimous: every single hand in the room -- all twenty-three of them -- goes up for the otter, and nobody votes for anything else.

Unanimous means fully in agreement from all parties -- every member, without exception. A single dissenting voice is enough to break it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

undivided: Undivided means not split into parts -- undivided attention, an undivided team. It describes wholeness of any kind, even one person's focus. Unanimous is stricter and belongs to votes and decisions: every single party said yes. A team can feel undivided while a formal vote still fails to be unanimous.

united: United means joined together behind a cause -- a united neighborhood, a united front. It describes general togetherness and allows a few quiet doubters. Unanimous is an exact count: in the actual vote, every voice without exception agreed. Fans stay united all season; only a vote can be unanimous.

unopposed: Unopposed means no one stood against it -- a candidate runs unopposed when nobody else enters the race, and silence or absence is enough. Unanimous demands more: every party actively agreed. A proposal can pass unopposed because half the room stayed home; unanimous means they all voted yes.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

divided: split into disagreeing groups

contested: argued over or challenged

Where it sits · how many people the agreement covers — widespread → unanimous → universal

widespread vs. unanimous: Widespread agreement is milder than unanimous -- widespread means most people are on board but a few may still object, while unanimous means every single vote, with no exceptions at all.

universal vs. unanimous: Universal goes even further than unanimous: a unanimous decision covers everyone in one room or committee, but universal agreement reaches everyone everywhere, far beyond a single vote.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — un(i)-

root — un(i)-: one (Latin unus)

root — anim-

root — anim-: mind, spirit (Latin animus)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin -osus)

Put it together

Put it together: Unanimous fuses Latin unus ('one') with animus ('mind, spirit'): 'of one mind.' A unanimous group has, for the moment, a single shared mind -- every member's judgment pointing the same way.

Use the root in a new word: animated

Root Check

Word Choice

Unanimous belongs to votes, verdicts, and decisions: a unanimous jury, unanimous approval, elected by unanimous consent. It is absolute -- 'nearly unanimous' means one or two held out, and a single 'no' unmakes it. For general togetherness without the strict all-count, 'united' serves better.
